comparison_rule: After committing all five hypotheses, compare each exact hypothesis with what implementation-3 requests and (if needed) its identified worker report. A match requires the same causal premise and corrective check; generic topical overlap or a number reservation is not a match. Keep literal match count separate from whether inputs are genuinely blind and are two failed fixes. Do not infer a missing target cause.

tasks.assumption: Moving lifecycle instructions into mods and testing their hook order is enough to make every real merge path run the intended observer/watch work before a sentinel is written.
tasks.check: In a throwaway workflow, run the real merge guard with pr empty and pr populated, force the observer check to fail, then inspect whether any pr-merge path still writes the merged sentinel or starts a second watch. Failure of either ordering refutes the premise.

quotes.quote: a failed observer check cannot stop `pr-merge`'s own scan from writing the sentinel

tasks.input_limit: The first report stopped before changing code; the second reports an amended implementation. These are not two failed fixes of one check.

tasks.assumption: A passing delivery check and a merge line pinned to the current head remain sufficient authorization until the head changes, even if a failure record or a grant changes at that same head.
tasks.check: After producing a passing head-pinned merge line in a throwaway repository, add a failure record or remove the grant without moving the product head; attempt the supported merge entrance and require refusal. A still-runnable line refutes the premise.

quotes.quote: prints a head-pinned merge line only for a class with a valid README grant
the printed merge line stays runnable after a later failure record or grant removal

tasks.input_limit: Dispatch 2 is an in-flight security-review message already covered by report 1. Report 2 is a later pin repair, so dispatch/report ordinals do not identify two sequential attempts.

tasks.assumption: Changing the brief or splitting the review by gate can make an unchanged reviewer find the same runtime write-limit defect when validation is confined to a diff that does not touch the responsible handlers.
tasks.check: On the saved design and validation diff, identify the public entrance and trace it to the session/comment write handlers; compare whether the existing validation review scope includes those handlers. If they are out of scope, another brief-only attempt cannot establish that runtime coverage; return the scope decision instead of patching the wording again.

quotes.quote: the brief cannot make the unmodified reviewer name the unbounded session or comment creation finding
the finding lives in handlers the diff does not touch and standard tier does not trace them

tasks.input_limit: Dispatch 2 only supplies a reserved ADR number. Report 2 already contains a gate-splitting amendment and a later validation replay; it is not a report of an independent second dispatched fix.

tasks.assumption: A latest representation, or just the newest addition of a dispatch-record path, is a sufficient proxy for all historical additions that the law must judge.
tasks.check: In a throwaway history, add a violating record, correct it, delete it, and re-add a corrected record at the same path; judge the original event and require it to stay a violation. Compare this with judging only the tip or newest add; either erasing the original violation refutes the premise.

quotes.quote: a later fix, deletion or sibling deletion must not clear a violation
a record deleted and re-added corrected at the same path leaves its first add unjudged

tasks.input_limit: Dispatch 2 only reserves an ADR number. Report 2 already describes fixes requested after external review; its cycle label is also cycle 1. Historical-event scope is an inference, not evidence that the first two dispatches were two failed fixes.

tasks.assumption: A syntactically recognizable Verdict/PASSED label is enough to recover the current validation decision, even when the label is qualified as prior or candidate lookup can fall back to an older passing section.
tasks.check: On throwaway report strings, put Prior Verdict: PASSED before the real Verdict: REJECTED, then put a same-head later REJECTED section over an older PASSED section and a latest PASSED without a candidate over an older one with a candidate. Require no current passing candidate in all three cases; accepting one refutes the premise.

quotes.quote: a qualified label (Independent Verdict: PASSED, Prior Verdict: PASSED) is accepted as the verdict
the latest section with a candidate still wins
the latest validation section with a counting Verdict form now decides
